question.prompt:
Let \(x_1,\) \(x_2,\) \(\ldots,\) \(x_n\) be a sequence of integers such that

(i) \(-1 \le x_i \le 2,\) for \(i = 1,\) \(2,\) \(3,\) \(\ldots,\) \(n\);

(ii) \(x_1 + x_2 + \cdots + x_n = 19;\) and

(iii) \(x_1^2 + x_2^2 + \cdots + x_n^2 = 99.\)

Let \(m\) and \(M\) be the minimal and maximal possible values of \(x_1^3 + x_2^3 + \cdots + x_n^3,\) respectively. What is \(\dfrac{M}{m}?\)

solutions.explanation:
Every term is one of \(-1,0,1,2\), so we can replace the sequence by counts of these four values. Let \(a,b,c,d\) be their respective counts. These are nonnegative integers, and zeros contribute nothing to any of the given sums. The conditions become
\[
-a+c+2d=19,
\qquad a+c+4d=99.
\]
Subtracting the first equation from the second gives \(a+d=40\). Substituting back gives
\[
a=40-d,
\qquad c=59-3d.
\]
Nonnegativity requires \(d\geq0\), \(d\leq40\), and \(3d\leq59\). Since \(d\) is an integer, these reduce to
\[
0\leq d\leq19.
\]
Conversely, every integer in this range gives nonnegative counts \(a=40-d\) and \(c=59-3d\), so the range is exact. The zero count \(b\) may be any nonnegative integer.

For \(-1,0,1\), cubing leaves the value unchanged. Each occurrence of \(2\) contributes \(8\) instead of \(2\), an increase of \(6\). Therefore the cubic sum is
\[
\sum_{i=1}^{n}x_i^3=19+6d.
\]
It is smallest at \(d=0\) and largest at \(d=19\). The first endpoint is realized by \(40\) copies of \(-1\) and \(59\) copies of \(1\). The second is realized by \(21\) copies of \(-1\), \(2\) copies of \(1\), and \(19\) copies of \(2\). These counts satisfy both original sum conditions; zeros can be added without changing them.

Thus \(m=19\), \(M=19+6\cdot19=133\), and
\[
\boxed{\frac{M}{m}=\frac{133}{19}=7},
\]
choice \(\boxed{\text{E}}\).
solutions.title: Count the four allowed values
